cards.explanation: The answer is that the king's son is dead. Joab, David's army commander (2 Samuel 8:16), gives the reason straight: "…because the king’s son is dead." The battle was won, but Joab sees that the news isn't simple for a father. He tells Ahimaaz, "You may do it another day…" This is a heavy part of the story, friends.

The answer is False. Ahimaaz does not drop the idea. He "persisted," and he asks Joab, "No matter what, please let me also run behind the Cushite!" Joab asks why he wants to run when he will not receive a reward. Ahimaaz answers, "No matter what, I want to run!"

The answer is "Then run." Joab says, "Then run!" Ahimaaz had said, "No matter what, I want to run!" and Joab lets him go. Joab had asked why he wanted to run with no reward coming, and Ahimaaz held firm.

The answer is outruns. The text says Ahimaaz "…ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite." The Cushite had set out first, and Ahimaaz still ended up ahead of him. Starting behind and finishing in front is a good feeling, friends.

The answer is that he brings good news. David says, "If he is alone, he bears good news." The watchman sees a man running alone and calls out to tell the king. To David, a lone runner points to good news.

The answer is True. The watchman calls out about another man running alone, and the king says, "This one also brings good news…" David uses the same rule again. A lone runner still means good news to him.

The answer is True. The watchman says the first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok. David answers, "This is a good man. He comes with good news." Ahimaaz is Zadok's son, and David speaks well of him before he even arrives.

The answer is that David asks, "Is the young man Absalom all right?" Absalom is David's son, the one who had been declared king in Hebron against him (2 Samuel 15:10). Ahimaaz brought news of victory, and the king asks about his son first. I think that tells you where his heart is.

The answer is False. Ahimaaz tells David, "…I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was." He doesn't say the king's son is dead, though Joab told him so (2 Samuel 18:20). David asked about Absalom, and Ahimaaz gave him no answer.
The answer is False. The question is the same. The king asks the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom all right?" He asked Ahimaaz those same words. The Cushite answers it where Ahimaaz didn't.

The answer is that Absalom is dead. The Cushite never says the word, but his wish makes it plain: "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man." Joab already said the king's son is dead (2 Samuel 18:20). David understands the answer.
The answer is the chamber over the gate. The text says the king "…went up to the chamber over the gate and wept." He was already sitting at the gate when the news came. He goes up to weep there.
The answer is died. David cries, "If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!" This is a father's grief, and it's heavy. In the same breath he calls out "My son, my son…"

The answer is mourning. The text says, "And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people…" They were told, "The king is grieving over his son." The whole mood of the day turns around.
The answer is True. The text says, "…the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice…" He is crying out his son's name, again and again. The people hear about it, and so does Joab.

The answer is that David loves those who hate him. Joab says, "You love those who hate you and hate those who love you!" Those are Joab's words to the king, and they're blunt. He says them to David face to face.
The answer is to go out and comfort his servants. Joab says, "Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants…" He wants David to go out to his men. Joab doesn't hold back, friends.
The answer is False. Joab says, "…I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight." Not half, but not a man. Joab doesn't go easy on the king.

The answer is True. The text says the people were told, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." Then "…they all came before the king." David has gotten up as Joab urged. Joab had told him, "Now therefore get up!"
